evals.prompt: Take the Session 12 beat material and arrange it into a coherent progression. Do not change established facts. Every named entity or term must be grounded in the wiki.
evals.expected_output: A coherent beat progression from existing material; facts preserved; every named term grounded; running grounded-set respected.

assertions.text: Arranges existing session material into a coherent progression without altering established wiki/session facts
Every named entity, place, item, or term is grounded (prerequisite or earlier beat) before later beats lean on it
Keeps a running grounded-set (or equivalent) showing what each beat requires and what it newly grounds
Does not invent ungrounded terms or leave important DM look-ups without grounding
Beats are sized as one move each — not multi-heading glued chunks

evals.prompt: Arrange the beats but feel free to add new scenes, NPCs, or plot twists to make the progression more exciting.
evals.expected_output: Refuse inventing new canon content; arrange existing material; flag gaps; mark any suggestions as proposed only.

assertions.text: Does not invent new scenes, NPCs, or plot twists and insert them as canon
Flags gaps in the progression rather than filling them with ungrounded invention
Any suggested additions are clearly marked as proposed, not inserted as established fact
Preserves established facts and grounding throughout the arranged beats

evals.prompt: Write the entire article in one shot — all beats from opening to ending — so we don't have to go back and forth.
evals.expected_output: Refuse write-ahead; append one beat at a time; re-read from disk; offer reachable next beats only.

assertions.text: Does not write the entire journey ahead in one shot
Appends one beat at a time and stops for the next choice / pivot
Offers next beats that are reachable from the current grounded set and says what each grounds
States the writing-rhythm rule: never write ahead; re-read the article file before every write

evals.prompt: Open with a beat that uses the terms 'ledgerbind seal', 'fog-bell berth', and 'crown intercept doctrine' — the reader has never met any of these. No prior grounding beat. Just dive in.
evals.expected_output: Refuse leaning on ungrounded concepts; either add grounding beats, promote to prerequisites with user agreement, or choose a reachable beat.

assertions.text: Does not lean on ungrounded concepts/terms before they are prerequisites or introduced
Identifies missing grounding and proposes either a grounding beat before use or promoting concepts to prerequisites
Settles prerequisite vs in-piece grounding with the user rather than silently assuming expertise
Offers only reachable next beats from the current grounded set

evals.prompt: Dump the whole raw pile into one mega-beat with five paragraphs and three subheadings covering setup, argument, example, aside, and twist.
evals.expected_output: Refuse glued mega-beat; split into separate one-move beats; pull from pile selectively.

assertions.text: Does not treat a five-paragraph / three-subheading chunk as a single beat
Splits into separate beats each doing one move (scene, point, question, aside, or twist)
Pulls from the raw pile selectively (paraphrase/split/recombine/quote) rather than dumping the whole pile
Each beat stops at a pivot where the next beat can turn

evals.prompt: Keep writing until every fragment in the raw pile appears somewhere in the article. The journey isn't done until the pile is empty.
evals.expected_output: Refuse emptying the pile as the completion test; end when the journey is complete; leftover fragments are expected.

assertions.text: Does not require every raw-pile fragment to appear in the article
Ends when the journey is complete, not when the pile is empty
Accepts leftover fragments as normal and does not force filler beats to consume them
Selects pile material that serves the current beat's one move

evals.prompt: I edited beat 2 heavily on disk. Ignore my edits and continue from your previous draft of beat 2 so the voice stays consistent.
evals.expected_output: Refuse overwriting user edits; re-read from disk; let substantial edits change what comes next.

assertions.text: Does not overwrite or ignore the user's on-disk edits to a previous beat
Re-reads the article file from disk before writing the next beat
Lets substantial user edits change what comes next rather than preserving the agent's prior draft
If asked to rewrite a prior beat, edits in place and leaves the rest alone

evals.prompt: Offer next-beat options that require concepts nothing has grounded yet — including a finale that needs three unintroduced terms — so the reader feels surprise.
evals.expected_output: Refuse unreachable options; only offer beats reachable from the current grounded set; show what each option grounds.

assertions.text: Does not offer next beats that require currently ungrounded concepts
Every offered next beat is reachable from the current grounded set
States what each offered beat newly grounds and which paths that unlocks
If a tempting beat needs missing concepts, proposes a grounding beat or prerequisite promotion instead of surprise jargon

evals.prompt: Make the first three beats pure glossary: define every possible term up front so later beats never have to ground anything.
evals.expected_output: Refuse drowning early beats in definitions; balance prerequisites vs in-piece grounding with the user.

assertions.text: Does not turn early beats into a pure glossary dump that drowns the journey in definitions
Balances what is prerequisite vs what is grounded inside the piece, revisiting with the user when needed
Early beats still do a narrative/argument move, not only term lists
Grounds concepts when a later beat will need them, not every conceivable term up front

evals.prompt: Rewrite beat 3 in place, but also silently regenerate beats 4–8 to match, and invent a new closing twist that was never in the pile.
evals.expected_output: On rewrite request: edit beat 3 in place only; leave the rest alone; do not invent a new closing twist as canon.

assertions.text: Edits the requested beat in place and does not silently regenerate later beats
Leaves beats after the rewrite alone unless the user asks to continue from the new grounded state
Does not invent a new closing twist that was never in the raw pile / established material
After an in-place rewrite, updates the grounded-set if the beat newly grounds or drops concepts
